small_guidance:
- The kernel is extremely slow (403ms) — BLOCK_M=128 with BLOCK_N inner loop forces the K-loop to re-load X tiles N/BLOCK_N times. Swap loop order: outer over K, inner over N, so X is loaded once per K-tile and reused across all N tiles. Even better, make K the outer accumulator over a single N tile per program.
- Add configs with larger BLOCK_K (64-128) and BLOCK_N=128/256, num_warps=8, num_stages=4 to better overlap K-loop loads on a 32768-deep K.
- Include `BLOCK_M` in the autotune key/configs (currently fixed at 128) and try BLOCK_M=64 with BLOCK_N=256 since M=128 is small relative to N=32768.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a standard 2D GEMM grid `(cdiv(M, BLOCK_M), cdiv(N, BLOCK_N))` writing per-tile partial sigmoid-sums into a temporary `(num_n_tiles, M)` buffer, then a tiny second kernel reduces along the n-tile axis. This exposes parallelism across N (currently only M=128 programs run, vastly under-utilizing the 4090's 128 SMs).
- Alternatively, split-K / split-N persistent kernel: launch ~128-256 programs each owning a (M-tile, N-slice), accumulate sigmoid-sum locally, then atomic-add into a length-M output. With M=128, N=K=32768 this exposes ~100x more parallelism than the current row-only grid.
- Transpose the weight to `(K, N)` once in `__init__` (store as buffer) so the inner GEMM loads W contiguously along N — current `tl.trans(w_vals)` plus strided loads on W's K-dim is suboptimal for this shape.
